limitations: A curated source snapshot, not a complete import graph, runtime trace, or execution order.
The sequential Gym integration is emphasized. Parallel execution, recovery, validators, recording, and planner internals are not exhaustively modeled.
References through protocols and injected factories are scoped to the described production assembly.
Source-reviewed means checked against the pinned source revision; it is not a physical qualification result.
Prototype overview imports cover selected source modules only. They do not establish runtime ordering or a complete dependency graph.

nodes.label: AtomicActionEngine
nodes.summary: Manages planning resources and atomic skills to create executable action sessions.
boundaries: Commands are dispatched by ExecutionRunner and its command sink.
nodes.details: Atomic Skills form the typed boundary between semantic intent and executable action plans. The engine owns planning resources and creates execution sessions. A runner and command sink dispatch commands; the engine itself does not advance the environment.

nodes.label: BaseEnv
nodes.summary: Owns the Gym loop, simulation initialisation, and environment step lifecycle.
boundaries: Simulation state advances through the environment lifecycle.
nodes.details: This is the common Gymnasium-compatible lifecycle beneath embodied tasks. It initializes the simulation manager and coordinates reset, stepping, and environment timing. Higher-level environments add task-specific scene assembly and behavior.

nodes.label: CLI
nodes.summary: Dispatches commands and lazily loads task discovery, environment, and training entry points.
boundaries: Task and runtime behaviour remain with their respective modules.
nodes.details: The unified embodichain command resolves a requested subcommand and loads its handler lazily. Use the CLI reference to find launch options for environments, training, assets, and other tools; task behavior stays in the handler-owned subsystem.

nodes.label: BufferedGymCommandSink
nodes.summary: Validates and buffers control commands for incremental Gym demonstration consumption.
boundaries: Accepting a buffered command does not mean the environment has stepped.
nodes.details: This sink validates and encodes runtime commands, then buffers controller actions for the Gym demonstration generator. It is the handoff between command dispatch and later environment consumption, rather than a direct call to simulation stepping.

nodes.label: CompiledTaskProgram
nodes.summary: Immutable compilation result with materialized task segments and analysis views.
boundaries: The result is not a control command or proof of successful physical execution.
nodes.details: The compiler expands the task into immutable, already materialized segments. Consumers can iterate those segments and inspect analyses before handing them to an execution integration. The object describes intended work, not its physical outcome.

nodes.label: Component composition
nodes.summary: Resolves environment and embodiment components into runnable Gym configurations.
boundaries: Deployment configurations cannot duplicate fields owned by selected components.

evidence.excerpt: """Resolve reusable environment and embodiment Gym components."""

nodes.details: Reusable environment and embodiment components separate physical scene ownership from robot, sensor, and Task Program selections. Composition resolves those selections into the deployment configuration and rejects duplicated component-owned fields.

nodes.label: Compute
nodes.summary: Shared numerical algorithms for kinematics, trajectories, geometry, and images.
boundaries: Does not depend on lab, simulation objects, or environment managers.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Array and tensor computations shared across simulation, planning, and tools.

Domain packages own their algorithms; private ``_warp`` packages contain Warp
implementations. Importing this package does not initialize a simulator or
load any computation backend."""

nodes.details: Compute provides reusable numerical routines for kinematics, trajectories, geometry, and images. Its dependency boundary excludes lab objects and environment managers, allowing higher-level robotics modules to share algorithms without owning their runtime lifecycle.

nodes.label: Config loader
nodes.summary: Loads deployment files, resolves components, and assembles the typed environment configuration.
boundaries: Configuration assembly precedes runtime creation. This module does not itself step the environment.
nodes.details: The loader decodes deployment files, resolves reusable components, and assembles typed environment configuration. It connects command-line inputs to environment construction, while leaving simulation stepping to the environment lifecycle.

nodes.label: Data pipeline
nodes.summary: Online data engine managing workers and their lifecycle.
boundaries: The data pipeline owns worker persistence and error propagation.
nodes.details: The online data workflow connects simulation producers with training consumers. An OnlineDataEngine manages shared trajectory data, while OnlineDataset exposes sampling through PyTorch dataset patterns. See the streaming guide for lifecycle, buffering, and sampling behavior.

nodes.label: Devices
nodes.summary: Base interfaces for real robot controllers.
boundaries: Device control and internal simulation objects have separate responsibilities.

evidence.excerpt: import abc  # for abstract base class definitions

nodes.details: Real-device controllers expose interfaces for physical robot deployment. They are owned separately from simulated Robot entities. The laboratory API reference documents the device layer and its relationship to the rest of the robotics package.

nodes.label: EmbodiedEnv
nodes.summary: Assembles scenes, managers, and demonstrations with optional Task Program integration.
boundaries: Language definitions, compilation, and semantic runtime belong to task_program.
nodes.details: Use this configuration-driven environment to assemble a robot task from scene objects, sensors, and manager-owned behavior. It extends the shared Gym lifecycle and optionally connects Task Program compilation and demonstrations through an environment adapter.

nodes.label: Environment launcher
nodes.summary: Runs task discovery, configuration loading, and Gym environment creation.
boundaries: Environment creation is dispatched through the registered Gym ID; task-specific behaviour stays with the environment.

evidence.excerpt: def cli(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None:

nodes.details: The run-env launcher discovers task packages, decodes the selected deployment, and creates the registered Gym environment. Use its launch guide to inspect a task, configure a run, and understand where configuration becomes a live environment.

nodes.label: TaskProgramEnvironmentAdapter
nodes.summary: Validates integration choices and assembles the semantic runtime and Gym bridge.
boundaries: Live data and concrete services are supplied by the environment factory.
nodes.details: This adapter connects the task language to a concrete environment. It validates the chosen integration and assembles the semantic executor, command buffer, shared clock, and demonstration bridge used by the Gym workflow.

nodes.label: ExecutionRunner
nodes.summary: Advances atomic skill sessions through observation, command, and clock interfaces.
boundaries: Command acceptance does not imply a completed physical state transition.
nodes.details: The runner advances an atomic session through observation, command, and clock interfaces. Its command sink determines where commands go. Acknowledgement of a command is distinct from confirmation that a physical effect has occurred.

nodes.label: TaskProgramDemoBridge
nodes.summary: Converts program segments into lazy Gym demonstrations with a shared runtime, buffer, and clock.
boundaries: This view focuses on sequential execution, not all parallel scheduling or recovery paths.
nodes.details: The bridge exposes program execution as incremental Gym demonstrations. It shares a buffered command sink and environment-step clock with the semantic runtime, so action consumption and time progression stay coordinated with the host environment.

nodes.label: Managers
nodes.summary: Organises observations, actions, rewards, events, and data recording within the environment lifecycle.
boundaries: Each manager defines the calling signature of its functors.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Managers that orchestrate collections of functors (observation, reward, event, action, dataset) running at specific points in the environment step loop.

Each manager owns a typed ``@configclass`` config whose attributes are ``FunctorCfg`` instances; the config attribute name becomes the functor's unique identifier.
"""

nodes.details: Managers organize task behavior around observations, actions, rewards, events, and dataset recording. Each manager invokes functors with its own contract, letting tasks compose behavior while sharing the environment reset and step lifecycle.

nodes.label: MotionGenerator
nodes.summary: Composes planning backends behind a unified robot motion generation interface.
boundaries: This entry point belongs to motion and is not re-exported by planners.
nodes.details: Use this entry point to turn joint or end-effector goals into timed trajectories. It composes planner backends behind one motion interface, while simulation playback or Atomic Skills consume the generated motion.

nodes.label: Physics backends
nodes.summary: Constructs the configured physics backend and connects simulation state to physics solving.
boundaries: Environment files declare default or newton; launch arguments do not switch backends.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Physics backend registry and factory.

Selects a concrete :class:`PhysicsBackend` from a physics config via
:func:`embodichain.lab.sim.cfg.physics_backend_from_cfg` and instantiates it
with the owning :class:`SimulationManager` as its back-reference.
"""

nodes.details: The physics layer constructs the backend selected by the environment file and connects scene state to physics solving. Default and Newton configurations have separate owners; a launcher can confirm the file selection but does not switch its backend.

nodes.label: Planners
nodes.summary: Provides motion planning backends that generate constrained robot trajectories.
boundaries: The MotionGenerator composition entry point belongs to the motion module.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Motion planning stack.

``BasePlanner`` trajectory planners (TOPPRA, trapezoidal, neural, and cuRobo)
produce joint trajectories from waypoints. Motion generation composes these
backends in ``embodichain.lab.sim.motion.motion_generator``.
"""

nodes.details: Planning backends produce robot trajectories with different timing, geometric, or collision constraints. Choose a backend through motion configuration; use MotionGenerator as the composition entry point when building a complete motion request.

nodes.label: TaskProgramCompiler
nodes.summary: Compiles task configuration into an analysable program using a static scene manifest.
boundaries: Program compilation and runtime semantic lowering are separate stages.
nodes.details: This is the static compilation stage. It validates a task against scene contracts and materializes bounded program segments. Runtime lowering remains a separate concern, so inspecting a compiled program does not require executing its robot actions.

nodes.label: RL training
nodes.summary: Organises policy learning, collection, evaluation, and model persistence.
boundaries: RL training interacts with simulation through the environment interface.
nodes.details: The reinforcement learning layer organizes algorithms, policies, rollout collection, training, evaluation, and model persistence. Training reaches simulation through the environment interface. Start with the RL overview for the roles and configuration of each part.

nodes.label: Robot
nodes.summary: Represents a simulated robot with control parts, joint state, and kinematics.
boundaries: Robot presets and live entity state are managed separately.
nodes.details: The robot facade exposes simulated joint state, control parts, and kinematic capabilities. SimulationManager creates and retains the live entity; robot presets and configuration describe how it should be assembled.

nodes.label: Scene generation
nodes.summary: Generates scene state from input images for scene asset workflows.
boundaries: Scene generation and simulation execution have independent lifecycles.
nodes.details: The Scene Engine turns image inputs into scene-state and asset workflows for simulation preparation. Scene generation has its own pipeline lifecycle; loading and executing the resulting scene in a simulation is a separate responsibility.

nodes.label: SemanticCallCompiler
nodes.summary: Analyses and lowers Semantic Calls against the bound scene and skill integration.
boundaries: Runtime semantic lowering is separate from static TaskProgramCompiler compilation.
nodes.details: Semantic Calls express high-level task intent. This compiler analyzes and lowers those calls against the bound scene and skill integration, keeping semantic interpretation separate from transport and environment stepping.

nodes.label: SemanticCallExecutor
nodes.summary: Lowers and executes semantic calls, creating an execution session for each call.
boundaries: Execution sessions do not span call boundaries.
nodes.details: At runtime, the executor lowers a call and starts an atomic execution session for its grounded invocation. It connects that session to observations, the selected command sink, and the execution clock through an ExecutionRunner.

nodes.label: Sensors
nodes.summary: Provides camera, stereo, and contact observations for the environment.
boundaries: Contact-data adaptation belongs to sensors; shared computation belongs to compute.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Sensors attached to the simulation scene.

``Camera``, ``StereoCamera``, and ``ContactSensor`` all derive from ``BaseSensor`` and expose batched ``TensorDict`` data buffers.
"""

nodes.details: Sensors turn simulation state into batched observations. Camera, stereo, and contact sensors expose different data contracts and configuration choices. Sensor-specific adaptation stays here, while reusable numerical image and geometry routines belong to compute.

nodes.label: SimulationTaskProgramFactory
nodes.summary: Binds simulated robots, planners, and services to construct the atomic skill engine.
boundaries: This simulation factory does not own runtime-independent program compilation.
nodes.details: The simulation factory supplies the concrete robot and planning services required by a Task Program integration. It resolves planner configuration, creates the motion generator, and constructs an atomic engine with the selected control profile.

nodes.label: SimulationManager
nodes.summary: Manages the world, robots, sensors, physics, and visualisation lifecycle.
boundaries: This explorer displays source relationships without starting the simulation runtime.
nodes.details: The simulation manager is the central owner of the simulated world. It creates and retains scene entities, coordinates physics and sensors, and starts optional browser visualization. Environment and task layers access the world through this API.

nodes.label: Solvers
nodes.summary: Provides inverse kinematics backends and stateful robot solving capabilities.
boundaries: Shared numerical algorithms belong to compute; stateful solvers remain in sim.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Inverse-kinematics solvers sharing the ``BaseSolver`` interface.

Provides analytic (SRS, OPW, UR), numerical (Pinocchio, Pink, Differential), and learning-based (PyTorch, NeuralIK) solvers, one per robot control part.
"""

nodes.details: Kinematic solvers map joint positions to poses and find joint positions for target poses. This layer contains robot-aware solver state and backend selection. Shared numerical routines belong to compute, while timed trajectories belong to motion planning.

nodes.label: EnvironmentStepClock
nodes.summary: Maintains execution time on the environment step grid.
boundaries: Time advances through the Gym bridge handshake; sleeping does not advance simulation.
nodes.details: Execution time is tied to the environment step grid. The Gym bridge and command sink use the same clock instance, allowing timing checks to stay aligned with the environment handshake instead of wall-clock sleeps.

nodes.label: Task discovery
nodes.summary: Imports installed task packages through entry points to populate the environment registry.
boundaries: Discovery is dynamic and depends on installed task packages; this view only links the official package.
nodes.details: Task discovery loads installed packages declared through the embodichain.tasks entry-point group. These imports populate the environment registry. The official task package is one selected example; actual discovery depends on the installed packages.

nodes.label: TaskProgramCfg
nodes.summary: Declarative task configuration describing intent and execution structure.
boundaries: Configuration alone does not execute a simulation.
nodes.details: Start here when describing an embodied task declaratively. The configuration records the program structure and targets that the compiler validates before execution; the same language can be supplied through JSON, YAML, or Python.

nodes.label: Official tasks
nodes.summary: Registers official task entry points and organises reusable robot tasks.
boundaries: Task configurations and Python registration entry points have separate owners.

evidence.excerpt:
"""Official task environments for EmbodiChain.

Importing this package triggers auto-registration of all task environments
via recursive module import. Each task-named module executes its
``@register_env`` decorator, registering the environment in gymnasium's global
registry.
"""

nodes.details: Official tasks are bundled in the same distribution under the embodichain_tasks import package. Import-backed tasks register during discovery, while supported configuration-defined Task Programs register when their Gym configuration is loaded.

nodes.label: Browser visualization
nodes.summary: Publishes simulation snapshots and interactive controls through a browser runtime.
boundaries: Simulation reads run on the simulation thread; backend updates run on the visualisation worker.
nodes.details: The browser runtime publishes simulation snapshots and interactive controls. Simulation reads remain on the simulation thread, while the visualization worker handles backend updates. This module visualizes a running world; this architecture explorer visualizes code structure.
